clinician.trajectory_summary: A female market worker in her 50s presented with 6 months of progressive fingertip pain and swelling that impaired her ability to handle goods. Physical examination revealed mild clubbing of both thumbs and index fingers without nail deformities. Imaging (radiography and MRI) demonstrated band acro-osteolysis of the distal phalanges of both thumbs and index fingers, with destructive changes in the distal interphalangeal joint of the right middle finger. Comprehensive laboratory workup excluded inflammatory (normal CRP), metabolic (normal alkaline phosphatase, calcium, PTH), and autoimmune causes (negative rheumatoid factor, anti-DNA, anti-Scl-70, anticentromere antibodies). Psoriatic arthritis was considered but ruled out due to absence of personal or family history of psoriasis, lack of typical psoriatic nail changes, and absence of dactylitis. After systematic exclusion of secondary causes, the diagnosis of idiopathic acro-osteolysis was assigned, though the final diagnosis statement notes this is 'likely suggestive of idiopathic form but is not conclusive.'
